name: August 11, 2026 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
Minutes
  Lakewood City Council
  Regular Meeting held
  August 11, 2026

MEETING WAS CALLED TO ORDER at 7:31 p.m. by Mayor Wood in the
Council Chambers at the Civic Center, 5000 Clark Avenue, Lakewood, California.

INVOCATION was offered by Dr. Fardad Mogharabi, Spiritual Assembly of the
Bahais of Lakewood

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE was led by Girl Scout Troop 70233

ROLL CALL: PRESENT: Mayor Jeff Wood
  Vice Mayor David Arellano
  Council Member Cassandra Chase
  Council Member Todd Rogers
  Council Member Rudy Villarreal

PUBLIC COMMENT ON ITEMS IN THE AGENDA – None

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS:

Mayor Wood 1) recognized Mary Alonzo on her 101st birthday, noting that he and
Vice Mayor Arellano had the opportunity to join Senior Center staff and residents
in celebrating her; 2) reported on his attendance at a) Lemonade Day held on
August 1, 2026, expressing appreciation to the Lakewood Jaycees for organizing
the event and providing young entrepreneurs with an opportunity to operate a
business and raise funds for charities of their choice; b) Lakewood Youth Sports
Awards Ceremony and Team Day; and c) National Night Out, further thanking
members of the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Los Angeles County
Fire Department, and Public Safety staff for their participation; and
3) congratulated newly promoted Captain Juan Briseno of the Lakewood Sheriff’s
Station.

Council Member Rogers 1) congratulated Captain Briseno on his promotion to
Captain of the Lakewood Sheriff’s Station; 2) recognized the outgoing
commissioners and expressed appreciation for their longstanding commitment to
the City; and 3) highlighted significant arrests made by the Lakewood Sheriff’s
Station, further expressing gratitude for the Sheriff’s Department’s hard work and
dedication to the City.

August 11, 2026

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS – Continued

Council Member Villarreal 1) reported on his attendance at the a) Southeast
Los Angeles County Workforce Development Board (SELACO WDB) meeting,
noting that he had the opportunity to showcase SELACO’s work to State Senator
Perez; b) Rotary Club of Lakewood and Project Shepherd’s annual summer
backpack giveaway assembly; c) F&M Bank’s 60th anniversary event; and
d) Lemonade Day; and 2) highlighted that he met with State Senator Gonzalez and
Assembly Member Solache to discuss community priorities and visions for the
future.

Council Member Chase 1) thanked the  Lakewood/Long Beach
Soroptimist International Club for its work in supporting women in the community
and region; 2) highlighted Lemonade Day, describing the event as a testament to
the leadership within the community and expressed appreciation to the Lakewood
Jaycees for organizing the event; and 3) recognized the outgoing commissioners
for their service to the City.

Vice Mayor Arellano 1) expressed appreciation to City staff and the Sheriff’s
Department for their continued efforts to keeping the community safe and clean;
2) highlighted recent events organized by the Recreation and Community Services
Department, noting that he received numerous compliments from residents and
looks forward to future community events; and 3) shared his pride in his daughters
for their accomplishments.

For the record, Mayor Wood introduced Captain Briseno, Lakewood Sheriff’s
Station, who provided a verbal report pertaining to Part 1 crimes.

Following discussion, 1) Council Member Rogers reiterated his appreciation for the
work of the Sheriff’s Department; 2) Council Member Chase expressed
appreciation for the work of the Sheriff’s Department, emphasizing that crime has
decreased in certain areas; 3) Vice Mayor Arellano noted that Lakewood Center
has been busier than in years past which may explain the slight increase in crime
in the subject area; 4) Council Member Villarreal stated that the City Council is
supportive of the Sheriff’s Department’s efforts, and expressed desire to see crime
decrease around the Lakewood Center; and 5) City Manager McCormack
explained that while crime has slightly increased, it is increasing at a slower rate
than in previous years.

1.1 COLLECTION OF NUISANCE ABATEMENT COSTS FOR 5557 GONDAR
AVENUE. [Continued from July 14, 2026]

Mayor Wood introduced the item.

Director of Community Development Cervantes 1) provided a verbal report of the
Agenda report; and 2) along with Deputy City Attorney Skolnik, responded to
Council Members’ questions and comments.

Following brief discussion, Mayor Wood opened the public hearing at 8:10 p.m.
and called for anyone in the audience wishing to address the City Council on the
matter.

For the record, City Clerk Wallace stated that no members of the public
participating remotely wished to address the City Council on this matter.

There being no one in the audience wishing to address the City Council on the
matter, Mayor Wood closed the public hearing at 8:11 p.m.

At the request of Vice Mayor Arellano, 1) Director Cervantes confirmed that a) staff
work with property owners to achieve compliance prior to placing a lien on a
property; and b) liens are collected upon the sale or transfer of property; and
2) Deputy City Attorney Skolnik confirmed that the property owner was aware of
the Public Hearing and is not in attendance.

For the record, Council Member Rogers explained that Code Enforcement
violations are often the result of complaints from neighbors, noting that the City
approaches these matters with compassion and works with property owners to
address concerns while ensuring they have the opportunity for due process;
however, the City has a responsibility to preserve the quality of life and protect the
well-being of all residents.

Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Rogers, seconded by
Vice Mayor Arellano, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to
adopt Resolution No. 2026-39 ordering the costs of abatement to be assessed as
a lien for $4,890 against the parcel of land commonly known as 5557 Gondar
Avenue, Lakewood, California:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Rogers, Villarreal, Arellano, Chase, and
  Mayor Wood

August 11, 2026

1.2 AUTHORIZE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF DC FAST CHARGING
STATIONS.

For the record, 1) Mayor Wood introduced the item; and 2) Director of Public Works
Pickler provided a verbal report of the Agenda report.

Following brief discussion, Mayor Wood opened the public hearing at 8:16 p.m.
and called for anyone in the audience wishing to address the City Council on the
matter.

For the record, City Clerk Wallace stated that no members of the public
participating remotely wished to address the City Council on this matter.

There being no one in the audience wishing to address the City Council on the
matter, Mayor Wood closed the public hearing at 8:17 p.m.

It was moved by Council Member Rogers, seconded by Vice Mayor Arellano, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to 1) conduct a public hearing
to consider adopting Resolution No. 2026-49 – A Resolution approving findings
pursuant to California Government Code Section 4217 for energy-related
improvements at the Nixon Maintenance Yard and authorizing the City Manager
to execute agreements for the purchase and installation of DC Fast Charging
stations and making related findings and determinations; 2) adopt Resolution No.
2026-49; 3) authorize the City Manager to enter into an energy services agreement
in the amount of $173,817 from the AB 2766 Air Quality Improvement fund with
Baker Electric & Renewables for installation of the charging stations at Nixon Yard,
in a form approved by the City Attorney; 4) authorize the City Manager to enter into
an agreement with Charge Harbor in the amount of $86,279 from the AB 2766
Air Quality Improvement Fund for the purchase of two ChargePoint Express 250
DC Fast Charging stations, including software support, activation, and warranty
services, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and 5) authorize a project
contingency from the AB 2766 Air Quality Improvement Fund in the amount of
$25,000:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Rogers, Villarreal, Arellano, Chase, and
  Mayor Wood

3.2 ADOPTION OF  THE  LAKEWOOD  ECONOMIC  DEVELOPMENT
STRATEGIC PLAN.

Mayor Wood introduced the item.

Director of Community Development Cervantes 1) provided a verbal report of the
Agenda report; 2) introduced John Keisler, Chief Executive Officer and
Managing Member, Sunstone Management, Inc., who provided a PowerPoint
presentation of the Agenda report; and 3) along with City Manager McCormack,
responded to Council Members’ questions and comments.

Following discussion, 1) Vice Mayor Arellano expressed support for the proposed
Economic Development Strategic Plan (Plan), stating that it would assist the
City with growth and help fill vacant business properties; 2) Council Member Chase
expressed support for the proposed Plan; 3) Council Member Rogers a) stated that
he is proud that the City is business-friendly, explaining that it is frustrating when
properties remain vacant; however, the City does not have control over a landlord’s
choice of tenant; and b) thanked staff for their work in maintaining quality customer
service; and 4) Council Member Villarreal expressed support for the proposed Plan
and encouraged residents to view it.
 City Council Minutes
August 11, 2026
Page 8

3.2 ADOPTION OF THE LAKEWOOD  ECONOMIC  DEVELOPMENT
STRATEGIC PLAN – Continued

For the record, Mayor Wood 1) requested the Plan be made available on the City’s
website; and 2) without objection, requested that the proposed
Economic Development Task Force Working Group (Task Force) a) consist of no
more than sixteen members; b) meet at least quarterly; and c) provide reports to
the City Council.

At the request of Mayor Wood, City Manager McCormack 1) confirmed that the
Plan would be made available on the City’s website; and 2) explained that staff will
bring forward proposed appointees and a draft scope of work for the Task Force
at a future meeting for City Council consideration.

For the record, Council Member Rogers 1) stated, without objection, that details
related to the proposed Task Force would be reviewed by the
Economic Development Committee, consisting of Council Member Chase and
himself, before returning to the City Council for consideration.; and 2) clarified that
the proposed Task Force is a non-Brown Act working group.

Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Wood, seconded by Council Member
Chase, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to 1) adopt the
Lakewood Economic Development Strategic Plan (2025-2030); 2) direct the
Community Development Department to use the Strategic Plan as the guiding
framework for setting priorities, developing programs, implementing the Enhanced
Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD), and reporting on performance over the
next five years; and 3) direct staff to return at the next City Council meeting with
appointments for the Economic Development Task Force Working Group:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Rogers, Villarreal, Arellano, Chase, and
  Mayor Wood

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Susan Singer, resident, 1) requested that Kay Ewing Donato, resident, be
allowed to speak on her behalf; 2) explained that she had conducted research on
Robert’s Rules of Order to identify suggestions that may help reduce stress and
assist speakers with disabilities in communicating more effectively; 3) stated that
she learned the City Council has researched the Americans with Disabilities Act
(ADA) and that ADA-related recommendations may take precedence over
Robert’s Rules of Order, subject to the discretion of the City Council, further
encouraging the City Council to consider implementing the suggestions discussed
and to further clarify equity and accessibility for individuals with disabilities; and
4) acknowledged and thanked the City for its efforts to accommodate residents
with disabilities.

Philip Norris, resident, 1) requested that the City provide more quantitative
measures and analysis in its reports and discussions; 2) questioned how frequently
residents are reporting issues compared to how many issues the City has identified
or addressed, further requesting that the City conduct additional analysis to
determine how enforcement and services can be applied equitably across all
communities; 3) expressed concerns about the City’s definition and enforcement
of commercial vehicles, noting that the City’s definition does not appear to include
the additional allowance for mirrors permitted under state law; 4) explained that
the City’s ordinance concerning residential trash containers specifies that
residents use twenty to forty gallon containers; however, many residents, including
himself, use the green trash containers provided by EDCO; 5) requested
quantitative analysis regarding the City’s response to homelessness, including
information concerning the thirty-three dedicated homeless services employees;
and 6) suggested the City communicate with the Los Angeles County Fire
Department regarding access routes to areas north of Carson Street to ensure
safety personnel are aware of the most appropriate routes.

Cindy Ehuan-Aila, resident, 1) submitted written materials for the record; and
2) expressed concerns regarding code enforcement and privacy compliance for
the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) located at 11868 209th Street.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business to be brought before the City Council,
Mayor Wood adjourned the meeting at 9:07 p.m. to Tuesday, September 8, 2026,
at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers.

Respectfully submitted,

Dakota Wallace, CMC
City Clerk
